paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. In this chapter, the people who cried out to God in battle are the same people who walked away from Him later. Look at what Chronicles says about the first group: "Because they put their trust in God, He answered their prayers." (1 Chronicles 5:20) Then look at the verdict on the second: "But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers…" (1 Chronicles 5:25)

Now hear this, because it matters. These were not nobodies. The family heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh were "mighty men of valor, famous men, and heads of their families." (1 Chronicles 5:24) Being strong, famous and a head of the family did not keep them faithful. A big résumé is not a big faith, and I say that as a stamper with a very small résumé.

So what do I take from it? Trust in God is not a one-battle thing. It's a daily thing, and it's the kind of thing you keep doing when nobody is shooting at you. Chronicles also says "the battle belonged to God" (1 Chronicles 5:22), so the victory was never theirs to start with. Keep your eyes on Him in the easy years too, baker, and keep those ovens ready.
